## My Reasoning

I have farmed this same land in Quzhou for over 50 years. My father did the same before me. Here in the North China Plain, there is really only one system that makes sense: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same fields. I know this rotation the way I know my own hands. I am not going to change what has worked.

I have about 8 mu of contracted land I still manage myself. At 70, I am slower than I was, but I hire machines for planting and harvesting — the cooperative has tractors and combines, and I pay them per mu. That way I do not break my back.

**Wheat (October through June):** I buy improved wheat seed from the township supply station — variety suited to Hebei, not the old landrace I used to save. I put down compound fertilizer (复合肥) as base dressing when I do rotary tillage before planting, then topdress urea at jointing stage. I irrigate three times: the pre-winter watering to get the roots set, again at jointing, and at heading. Three times is what my neighbors do, what my father did, what I know is right for this land. I spray herbicide in early spring and a fungicide before heading to keep powdery mildew and rust off.

**Maize (June through September):** Right after the wheat combine comes through, I call the seeder to plant maize directly into the stubble — no tillage, saves water and time. I use hybrid seed, same as everyone here now. Maize gets summer rain so I only pump once, usually in July if it stays dry too long. I spray herbicide at emergence and watch for corn borer — spray once if I see damage.

I am not planting cotton anymore. The price is too uncertain and my knees cannot handle the picking. Wheat and maize, I know the costs, I know the buyers, I know what to expect.
